concept: TagInput is the Input window with the typed words kept inside it. Each word becomes a removable Chip standing in the well, and the caret follows the last one, so the whole value of the field sits in one place to read. Enter or a comma turns the text into a chip, Backspace on an empty field takes the last one back.
family_difference: TagInput lets the well wrap onto more rows, holds removable Chips before the caret, and turns text into a chip on Enter or comma instead of keeping one string.

default_to_avoid.pattern: tag input built as a bordered 8px box with 24px pills, each holding a 12px cross
default_to_avoid.why_not: A 12px cross is not a part a finger can hit and the bordered box floats on the page, while dial's chips keep a 44px remove key inside a recessed well.

default_to_avoid.pattern: tag input that adds a tag on every blur with no word and no message when it refuses a duplicate
default_to_avoid.why_not: A silent refusal leaves the person guessing why nothing happened, so every refusal is spoken in words and announced.

references.source: Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): the entry window is a recess in the body, and what was keyed in stays visible in it
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): the chosen bands stay latched down in a row beside the dial
system/FORM.md input class: recessed well, full width of its column, label printed above on the inset line

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The well is surface.sunken with elevation.well like Input, and the chips stand up out of it as raised parts, so the typed words read as keys in a recess.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line
derivation.form: The label, well and messages stack in one column on the inset line, and the well keeps the full inline size of that column however many chips it holds.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: Each chip is 44px tall with its own remove key, the text field is 44px tall, and the rows of a wrapped well keep a gap so no two targets touch.

derivation.consequence: and a visible value and label
derivation.form: Enter and comma add, Backspace on an empty field removes the last chip, Tab reaches each remove key, and the value is the chips themselves, with a hint and a spoken line for every add, removal and refusal.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: A chip appears and leaves at once, with no slide, so nothing in the well moves except the row the caret is on.

options.name: chips inside the well, caret after the last
one-row well with the chips standing beneath
tags as ruled rows under the well

variants.reason: A keeps the value and the entry in one recess, so the person looks in one place; B splits the entry from its result and leaves the well looking empty, and C reads as an ordered list, which is Queue's job.

root.why: The field stacks its label, well and messages in one column so the label sits on the inset line above the well.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, and it also names the text field and the list of chips.

well.why: The recess takes the inverse light and wraps its chips onto new rows so every word stays visible without scrolling.

list.why: The chips form a named list so a screen reader says how many tags there are, while the list adds no box of its own.

item.why: Each tag is one list item that adds no box, so its 44px chip sits in the well's own row grid with a gap on every side.

field.why: Typed text is primary ink on the sunken plastic at more than 4.5:1, with a line box tall enough for Thai marks, and it takes the rest of the row after the last chip.

hint.why: The hint is secondary ink in the caption size under the well and says which keys add and remove.

error.why: The refusal or error is critical red with a glyph and words, never orange and never colour alone.

glyph.why: A printed mark beside the words means a refusal is never told by colour alone, for people who cannot see the red.

focus-within.why: The well shows the same dark ring as every part when the text field or a remove key holds the keyboard focus.

data-invalid=true.why: An invalid well draws its edge in the critical red, which is never orange, and the message below names the problem.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled field loses its recess shadow and its text fades to half, and its chips flatten, so it reads as not taking input.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the well keeps a real border and the focus ring uses the system highlight colour.
